decision: preserve the waitlist site plus the guarded Stripe success flow
why: existing paid-session links may still rely on the server verification route

decision: use npm workspaces with the current app under apps/web
why: supports future apps without introducing a task runner or premature shared package

decision: record the dependency installation failure before editing
why: the original locked app cannot be tested until the local npm client issue is bypassed

decision: select a static-first apps/web capsule with two Stripe server functions
why: three independent sketches converged and this shape keeps the public surface and call chain smallest

decision: port the application to TanStack Start under apps/web and remove the Next.js delivery path
why: one application capsule preserves behavior while establishing the workspace boundary

decision: prerender only the public home route and keep the paid success route dynamic
why: private Stripe verification cannot be captured in a static artifact
evidence: npm run check && npm run build

decision: pin the Worker to Cloudflare account 32967fffa44c1d38bc86ab6e4e419edb
why: Wrangler has access to two accounts and non-interactive deployment must be deterministic

decision: bootstrap yatb-web on workers.dev without placeholder payment secrets
why: Cloudflare cannot create a new Worker with declared required secrets before their values exist

decision: keep production DNS on Vercel until Stripe secrets are installed in Cloudflare
why: cutting over now would break valid paid-session success links

decision: preserve session_id at the URL boundary and attach no-store headers to redirect responses
why: independent review found TanStack normalization duplicated the bearer token and added a redundant redirect

decision: upgrade checkout and setup-node actions to v7
why: the first pushed run passed but GitHub reported that the v4 actions use the deprecated Node 20 runtime

decision: delegate youraveragetechbro.com to Cloudflare while retaining the imported Vercel web records during propagation
why: traffic stays recoverable on Vercel until the Worker and Cloudflare zone are ready

decision: store only STRIPE_SECRET_KEY as an encrypted secret and track STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID as a Worker variable
why: the key grants account access while the price ID is a public resource identifier

decision: replace the Vercel apex and www records with Worker custom domains and redirect the apex to www
why: the application now runs entirely on Cloudflare while preserving the canonical hostname and URL suffixes

decision: probe Stripe with a synthetic checkout session through the production Worker
why: Stripe returned the expected missing-session error, proving the encrypted credential authenticates without exposing paid onboarding data

decision: declare both production custom domains in Wrangler configuration
why: subsequent deploys now reproduce the Cloudflare routing topology instead of relying on dashboard-only state
